title: Generic flatness and local finite presentation over a reduced affine scheme
statement: Let $g:U\to V$ be a morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose $V$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and $g$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There is an open subscheme $D\subseteq V$ [def-weil-open-immersion] whose underlying subset is dense in $V$ such that $U\times_VD\to D$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No Noetherianity or irreducibility is assumed; the empty affine scheme is allowed as source or target.

source.place: Tag 052B (proposition-generic-flatness-reduced), structure-sheaf case for affine source and affine reduced target. A locally finite type map between affine schemes is quasi-compact and hence finite type; only the local finite-presentation part of the conclusion is asserted.

proof.text: Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and $g=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$. The ring $A$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to the whole affine source and target shows that $B$ is a finite type $A$-algebra. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], choose $n\geq0$ and a surjective $A$-algebra map $q:P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$.

Through $q$, the $P$-module $B$ is generated by $1$: every $b\in B$ equals $q(p)\cdot1$ for a lift $p\in P$. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-polynomial-module-generic-freeness] to this cyclic module. It gives a dense open $D\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$, the union of the $D(f)$ for which $B_f$ is free over $A_f$ and finitely presented over $P_f=A_f[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. For every $y\in D$, choose such an $f$ with $y\in D(f)\subseteq D$. Here localization of the underlying $A$-module of $B$ is the same fraction module as the underlying module of $B[1/\varphi(f)]$: both use fractions $b/\varphi(f)^a$ and the identical equality relation.

source.place: Tag 051Z (lemma-generic-flatness-reduced), polynomial-module case and the last paragraph passing from polynomial algebras to arbitrary finite type algebras; apply only the polynomial-module case here.

proof.text: Fix a good $f$. Evaluation gives $q_f:P_f\to B_f$; it is surjective, since a fraction $b/\varphi(f)^a$ is the image of $f^{-a}p$ for any $p\in P$ with $q(p)=b$. Regard $q_f$ as a $P_f$-linear map. Its source is generated by $1$ and its target is finitely presented by step 2. Thus [lem-trf-finite-presentation-surjective-module-kernel] says that $\ker q_f$ has finitely many $P_f$-module generators $h_1,\ldots,h_m$. Since this kernel is an ideal, the same $h_j$ generate it as an ideal. Sending the class of $p$ to $q_f(p)$ now gives a bijective $A_f$-algebra map $A_f[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(h_1,\ldots,h_m)\to B_f$: surjectivity is that of $q_f$, and a class maps to zero exactly when its representative is in its kernel. This is a finite algebra presentation by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra].

source.place: Tag 051Z (lemma-generic-flatness-reduced), final polynomial-to-algebra reduction; Tag 0519 (lemma-extension), part (5), applied to P_f -> B_f.

proof.text: For the same good $f$, step 2 also gives that $B_f$ is a free $A_f$-module. By the explicit free-module clause of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], $B_f$ is flat over $A_f$.

source.place: Tag 051G (lemma-local-artinian-characterize-flat), proof: every free module is projective and every projective module is flat; applied to the freeness from Tag 051Z.

proof.text: For any open $D\subseteq V$, the inverse-image open $g^{-1}D$ with restricted sheaf represents $U\times_V D$. Indeed a pair of maps $T\to U$, $T\to D$ with equal composites into $V$ gives a unique map into $g^{-1}D$: the first map has image there, and its map of sheaves restricts to the restricted sheaf. Conversely a map into $g^{-1}D$ gives that pair. These constructions are inverse and preserve the projections, so [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies the restriction map $g_D:g^{-1}D\to D$ with the required base change. Open subschemes and the restricted sheaves are as in [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 052B (proposition-generic-flatness-reduced), notation X_U; the universal property of restriction to an open subset.

proof.text: For a good $f$, [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-pullback] identifies $g^{-1}D(f)$ with the principal open $D(\varphi(f))$ of $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], these are affine opens with coordinate rings $B_f$ and $A_f$ respectively. Their induced section map is $A_f\to B_f$, $a/f^k\mapsto\varphi(a)/\varphi(f)^k$: restrictions send $a/1$ to $\varphi(a)/1$, and a ring map sends an inverse to the inverse of its image. Step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] therefore show that $g^{-1}D(f)\to D(f)$ is flat. Step 3 supplies its finite affine algebra presentation.

Take the dense open $D$ of step 2, equipped with its open subscheme structure. For any $x\in g^{-1}D$, choose a good $f$ containing $g(x)$ as in step 2. The affine neighbourhoods $g^{-1}D(f)$ of $x$ and $D(f)$ of $g(x)$ lie inside $g^{-1}D$ and $D$. Their finite algebra presentation proves local finite presentation at $x$ by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Their flatness from step 6 says exactly that the local-ring map at $x$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Restriction to open subschemes leaves these local rings and this map unchanged by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Hence $g_D$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. If $V$ is empty, step 2 gives $D=\varnothing$, dense in the empty space, and all pointwise assertions are vacuous; an empty source likewise causes no exception. Step 5 gives the asserted properties of $U\times_V D\to D$.

source.place: Tag 052B (proposition-generic-flatness-reduced), concluding paragraph, and the pointwise definitions Tags 01TP and 01U3.

proof_origin.place: Tag 052B (proposition-generic-flatness-reduced), specialized to the single affine source chart and the structure sheaf; its algebraic input Tag 051Z is reduced to the polynomial-module case as in the final paragraph of that lemma.
